summary: Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian who earned degrees from Calcutta, SOAS, and Cambridge under scholars including Arthur Llewellyn Basham and H. W. Bailey. He served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta from 1975 to 1998.

A scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, Brendan Ozawa-de Silva completed doctorates at the University of Oxford and Emory University. He taught as an Associate Professor at Life University (2012–2017) and an Associate Teaching Professor at Emory (2022).

A scholar of linguistics, Indology, and philosophy, Brendan S. Gillon studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1974 to 1981. Around 1992, he served as Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University.

A scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, Bret W. Davis studied at Vanderbilt and Kyoto Universities. He held research and teaching posts in Japan before serving as Assistant and later Associate Professor of Philosophy at Loyola University Maryland (attested 2007–2018).
Brian Bocking is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Michael Pye and earned his PhD at the University of Leeds, attested in 1984.
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1963–1967) and trained under Geshe Wangyal from around 1967 to 1973.

Brian D. Ruppert specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1998–2018) before becoming Professor of Japanese Studies at Bates College around 2018.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history, Brian Daizen Victoria earned degrees from Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa, and Temple Universities. His academic career includes posts at the University of Auckland, Antioch University, and a fellowship at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Central Asian history and Buddhist studies, completing his PhD under György Kara at Indiana University Bloomington in 2005. By 2026, he was a Mongolian Language Program Lecturer at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Haileybury and Fort William College. He spent his career in diplomatic service, serving as British Assistant Resident and Resident at the Court of Nepal between 1820 and 1843.

Brian J. Nichols is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD at Rice University under Anne Carolyn Klein (attested 2011) and studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies.

Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Cape Town and University College London. A co-founder of the EASAS and the Ancient India and Iran Trust, she was also a Fellow of Wolfson College, Cambridge (1982–2017).
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna, where she subsequently served as an associate university professor around 1997.
Brigitte Steinmann is a scholar of Tibetology who studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and Bahadur Singh. She held a post at the University of Montpellier, attested in 2004.

Brij Kishor Tripathi worked in Indology and Tibetology as a research assistant at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1995) and held mathematics teaching posts at institutions including KNIT, CIPET, and L.D. College of Engineering (2018).

Bronislav Ivanovič Kuznecov was a Tibetologist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1951 to 1956 under Boris Ivanovich Pankratov and Vladimir Svjatoslavovič Vorob’ëv-Desjatovskij. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University in 1959.

Bronisław Malinowski studied at the Jagiellonian University, Leipzig, and the London School of Economics under Wilhelm Wundt, C. G. Seligman, and Edvard Westermarck. He held a chair in anthropology at the LSE (1922–1938) and a professorship at Yale (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Melbourne, Sydney, and Auckland under Rosalind Hursthouse and John Bishop. She served as Assistant Professor at Marquette University (2012–2014) before becoming Associate Professor at the Australian National University in 2014.

Brook Ziporyn is a scholar of sinology, philosophy, and religion who studied at Chicago and Michigan. He taught at Northwestern University (~1999–2012) before becoming the Mircea Eliade Professor at the University of Chicago around 2013.

Brooke Foss Westcott was a scholar in religious studies who was educated at King Edward's School and Trinity College, Cambridge. He later served in an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1870 to 1890.
